source: NACA Report 747, figures 8, 9 (four-blade single rotation: two 2-blade hubs in tandem, co-rotating) and 11, 12, 13 (four-blade dual rotation; 12 gives front and rear CP separately), no wing; digitized with tools/digitize.py. Only the attached-flow branches (descending in V/nD, below the stall humps) were traced.
notes: Figures 9c, 13a and 13b: the first digitization anchored CP = 0 on the lowest grid line inside the crop, which was one line above the axis; values were raised by one grid step (0.05, 0.01, 0.02). Checked against the axis labels and against the report's efficiency curves (figures 7 and 10).
Figure 9c: the crop also missed the J = 0 grid line, so J was raised by one grid step (0.1); checked against the V/nD labels (the 50 deg curve meets CP = 0.18 at J = 2.95).

Figure 12 (individual CP, front solid, rear dashed): solid and dashed ink separated by connected-component length; front curves traced, rear read from dashed pixels nearest (figure 13 total - front) within 0.012, kept only where dashes are visible (they merge into the solid where the curves touch). The dashed readings agree with total - front to 0.002 on average, which also confirms the figure 13 corrections.
Figure 13c (dual 50 deg total CP) uses a piecewise-linear y calibration between grid lines: the scan is stretched by up to 4 px there.

peak_efficiency.note: Peak efficiency read by eye from figures 7 (single) and 10 (dual), +-0.005.
